description: We are a team of passionate learners driven by curiosity, creativity, and innovation. We believe in teamwork and problem-solving, and aim to turn ideas into impactful solutions through the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary:
VITALIS – Vitality Intelligence & Tracking for Astronaut Life in Space

VITALIS is an intelligent astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support the physical and behavioral well-being of astronauts during long-duration space missions. It provides a centralized system to track important health indicators, identify potential health risks, and help astronauts make informed decisions about their well-being.

The platform addresses the challenges of spaceflight, including radiation exposure, altered gravity, isolation, and confinement, which can contribute to changes in cardiovascular health, bone density, immune function, and mental well-being. By organizing health data, monitoring health trends, and highlighting concerning changes, VITALIS helps astronauts recognize potential health issues and take timely action.

The importance of VITALIS lies in enabling greater health awareness and supporting independent health management when immediate medical assistance from Earth may be limited. It aims to make long-duration space exploration safer, more informed, and more sustainable by putting astronaut health at the center of every mission.
details:
**VITALIS – Crew Health Monitor**

Vitalis is a web-based health monitoring platform designed to help astronauts monitor their physical and mental well-being during long-duration space missions. Space environments expose astronauts to challenges such as radiation, altered gravity, isolation, and confinement, which can affect cardiovascular health, immunity, bone strength, sleep, and mental health.

Our solution provides a centralized dashboard where astronauts can record their daily health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, sleep duration, exercise, radiation exposure, mood, stress levels, and symptoms.

The system evaluates these inputs across five major health domains: Cardiovascular, Immune, Bone & Muscle, Radiation, and Behavioral health. It uses rule-based assessment logic to classify health conditions into three levels: Normal, Watch, and Act. It also tracks health trends over time, compares readings against personal baselines, highlights potential concerns, and provides suggested follow-up actions.

Vitalis offers several benefits, including early identification of unusual health patterns, improved health awareness, continuous self-monitoring, and better communication between astronauts and ground medical teams through generated health summaries.

The prototype is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with browser localStorage for saving daily health records. It also includes an interactive dashboard, health trend summaries, a 21-day demonstration dataset, and medical report generation.

The innovative aspect of Vitalis is its combination of multiple health indicators into one simple, astronaut-centred platform. Instead of displaying isolated measurements, it focuses on personal health trends and understandable alerts, helping astronauts take a more proactive approach to their health.

Our long-term vision is to extend Vitalis with wearable-device integration, secure data synchronization, and improved health analytics to support safer and more informed long-duration human space exploration.
dataRefs: Vitalis was built with AI.The health domains follow the hazards listed in the challenge brief. Thresholds are illustrative defaults and were not derived from or validated against NASA documents. They would need review by qualified flight medical staff.
